docs.text: ProxiomeVis R ProxiomeVis is an R Shiny explorer for processed Pixelgen data. It combines prepared cell annotations and embeddings with frozen abundance, self-proximity, and colocalization results from the tertiary analysis. The app provides: QC cell counts and stored cell annotations; interactive embeddings colored by annotation or marker abundance; per-sample summaries, donor-specific contrasts, and stored cross-donor descriptive effects for the three readouts; downloadable tables for the currently displayed stored results; bounded background comparisons on selected cells within one donor/cell type; on-demand, node-only 3D cell views with marker-identity highlights. The app does not open PXL files or recalculate proximity scores. A preparation workflow builds a compact plain-R bundle and optional disk-backed proximity and graph sidecars. Sessions share the startup bundle read-only within each R process; analysis workers load only a bounded selection of observed scores. The graph sidecar uses one Parquet file per sample and a version 3 index. Arrow selects one cell's nodes for viewing; no edges or marker-count matrices are stored there. Interpretation boundary The demo contains two donors. Combined donor-matched effects are descriptive, contain no p-values, and are not population-level inference. Donor-specific report volcanoes reproduce stored exploratory component-level p-values from the tertiary analysis; Shiny does not recalculate them. Cells are not independent biological replicates. Start with Getting started , then review the precomputed-results contract and hybrid analysis guide before preparing a new dataset.

docs.text: Getting started Run commands from the ProxiomeVis directory. The Cell 3D renderer uses the CRAN threejs package (>= 0.3.4): install.packages("threejs") . Plotly remains in use for the other interactive plots. 1. Prepare the demo RDS The repository expects the demo source at ../pixelgen_demo_data . Build the runtime file from its CCA object and tertiary results: Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_precomputed_rds.R \ ../pixelgen_demo_data/demo_analysis/cca_analysis/results/demo_cca_clustered.rds \ ../pixelgen_demo_data/demo_analysis/tertiary_analysis \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds The source tree is read-only. The script creates or replaces only the explicit output path after validating the source object and frozen tables. 2. Prepare the hybrid application bundle OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ARROW_NUM_THREADS=1 \ Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds output/hybrid_demo This exports a plain-R analysis.rds , observed proximity rows in proximity/ , and node-only 3D tables in graphs/ : one Parquet file per prepared sample and a version 3 index.rds . Each row contains a cell ID, 3D coordinates, and marker identities; no edges or marker counts are exported. Rerunning reuses validated completed sample files. Existing version 2 graph sidecars remain readable, but upgrading to the smaller version 3 files requires preparation in a new output directory. Supply the source PXL directory as the optional third argument if paths moved. Keep the bundle and sidecar directories together when copying to a server. To prepare 3D assets for only one or a few cells, supply a fourth argument: a text file containing one exact cell ID per line, with no header, blank lines, or duplicates. The third argument must be the PXL directory: Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds output/hybrid_selected \ ../pixelgen_demo_data/data/nf_pixelator_outdir/pixelator graph_cells.txt Only graph preparation is restricted by this list; the analysis bundle and proximity sidecar still cover the dataset. Cell 3D shows prepared-cell coverage; ranked cells without an asset are labeled and cannot be displayed. Rerunning with additional cells atomically rewrites each affected sample file with the union of old and new cells and updates the graph index. Previously prepared cells are retained. Run preparers sequentially, not concurrently against the same directory. Omit the fourth argument to prepare all cells, or call build_hybrid_bundle(..., graphs = FALSE) from R to omit graph preparation. Old version 1 per-cell graph RDS exports are not compatible with this reader. Preserve that directory and rebuild into a new output directory, then deploy the new bundle and sidecars together. No automatic destructive migration is performed. 3. Start Shiny The default input is output/hybrid_demo/analysis.rds when it exists, falling back to output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds : Rscript --vanilla -e 'shiny::runApp(".", host="127.0.0.1", port=3838)' Open http://127.0.0.1:3838 . To use another trusted prepared file: export PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS=/absolute/path/to/results.rds Rscript --vanilla -e 'shiny::runApp(".", host="127.0.0.1", port=3838)' Plain bundles require no Seurat/PNA class packages for viewing. Legacy inputs still require those packages; new statistical tests require the analysis-worker dependencies listed in the README. Cell 3D requires arrow and dplyr in the Shiny R environment. No runtime PXL mount is required. The app loads the configured RDS once and does not expose a visitor-selectable server path. For trusted local administration only, set PROXIOME_ALLOW_LOCAL_LOAD=true before startup to show the path field inside the upper-right Dataset panel. Never enable that setting on a public deployment. 4. Explore or run a new comparison Use the top navigation for Overview / QC , Embeddings , Precomputed results , Custom analysis , and Cell 3D . Open Dataset at the upper right for the active bundle and configured sidecars. In Precomputed results , choose one donor, cell type, comparison, and readout once. A single-donor dataset shows a fixed donor label instead of a redundant dropdown. The shared selection persists across these subtabs: Summary: stored differential-effect heatmap, optionally across all cell types; the original abundance heatmap is available in a collapsed section. Volcano: donor-specific stored test with hover, feature selection, and zoom. Spatial matrix: interactive self-proximity and colocalization together, with condition-profile and differential-effect views. Tables & methods: searchable results, sample support, original method settings, and CSV downloads. Volcano and spatial views need one cell type; they do not silently substitute one when All cell types (summary) is selected. Controls select stored rows, never rerun a test. Positive effects mean target minus reference. Stored component-level P values are exploratory within one donor, not population-level treatment inference. Spatial condition means are not the group medians used for stored differential effects. Click a plot feature or result-table row to update the shared selected-feature panel. Self-pairs and reversed marker pairs refer to the same feature. Condition values appear only when they were actually stored. Explore cells in 3D transfers the donor, cell type, and pair without loading a graph. FDR and search controls filter tables and their Filtered table CSV downloads. All stored rows CSV retains every stored row in the chosen scope, ignoring those filters. Report plots and Original report SVG retain the original thresholds; heatmap controls change only the summary display. Hidden plots are not rendered until needed, and precomputed views require no sidecar reads. Use Custom analysis for a new selected-cell comparison: choose one donor, one cell type, two conditions and markers; optionally lasso cells in the embedding; acknowledge the exploratory scope and click Run comparison . You can navigate while the separate R process works or cancel it. Export results and their JSON provenance. Report tabs remain unchanged. Missing spatial sidecars disable only spatial reanalysis, not the report viewer. Use Cell 3D to rank cells within donor, cell type, and condition by two markers' observed log2 ratio (self-pairs allowed; pair order does not matter). After a feature handoff, choose a condition from the comparison and one highlight marker. Choose a ranked cell, then click Display to load it. Changing controls does not update the displayed graph until Display is clicked. Rotate, zoom, hover, and export its nodes and provenance. The view is nodes only, and all nodes remain visible unless the cell exceeds the 200,000-node limit. Coverage is shown explicitly. Initial access may checksum the whole sample file; later cell queries use Arrow row-group pruning and cached checksum validation. Coordinates represent a graph layout, not physical microscopy positions, and marker highlights indicate identities rather than counts or a colocalization test. Read Hybrid analysis before interpreting new P values. Tests Rscript --vanilla tests/testthat.R Synthetic fixtures include small PXL-like databases and background-worker tests; CI does not need the original PXL files or the demo dataset.

docs.text: Prepared reports and new exploratory analyses The application separates three operations: viewing frozen results, submitting a bounded new comparison to an R worker, and opening prepared cell graphs. Viewing or filtering a report never changes its stored statistics. Runtime analysis reads a prepared proximity sidecar, not PXL files. Running a new comparison Open the exploratory-analysis tab, choose one donor, one cell type, two distinct conditions, a readout, and the markers to test. Use all cells in that scope, or select a subset using the embedding's lasso/box tools or the cell selector. The selected conditions assign cells to target and reference groups; cells cannot belong to both. The displayed counts update before submission. Confirm the exploratory-analysis notice and click Run comparison . An R process performs the test while the reports remain usable. Changing controls does not rerun a test. The result identifies the submitted scope; downloads include the results CSV and JSON provenance with the exact selected cell IDs. The volcano supports hover, box/scroll zoom, and double-click reset. The results table also includes requested features that could not be tested. Only one background analysis runs at a time per application process. The server limits each request to 2,000 cells, 160 markers, 1,000 unordered non-self pairs, and 1,000,000 retained score rows, with a 120-second timeout. Colocalization tests all combinations of the chosen markers: 45 markers produce 990 pairs; 46 exceed the cap. Oversized selections are rejected, not silently downsampled. Cancel a running job or narrow the cells/markers if it exceeds a limit. Methods and interpretation Readout Effect: target minus reference Test and minimum support Abundance Mean stored normalized abundance pixelatorR::RunDAA , using Seurat's two-sided Wilcoxon test; at least 3 selected cells per group Self-proximity Median observed log2_ratio for each marker paired with itself pixelatorR::DifferentialProximityAnalysis(metric_type = "self") ; at least 20 retained observations per marker in each group Colocalization Median observed log2_ratio for each unordered pair of different markers pixelatorR::DifferentialProximityAnalysis(metric_type = "co") ; at least 40 retained observations per pair in each group Abundance uses the bundle's existing transformed layer without renormalization: mean_fxn = Matrix::rowMeans , fc_name = "difference" , slot = fc.slot = "data" on a temporary assay containing those stored values, min.pct = 0 , test.use = "wilcox" . RunDAA sets logfc.threshold = 0 and applies BH correction to the returned marker p-values. The demo layer contains CLR abundance. Three cells is the API's testing minimum, not evidence that a small comparison is well powered; the original pipeline recommends 20 for abundance. Spatial tests use the package's two-sided, tie-corrected rank test with continuity correction. The effect is a difference of median log2 ratios , not the log fold-change in mean abundance. The preparation formula is log2(pmax(join_count, 1) / pmax(join_count_expected_mean, 1)) . BH adjustment is performed separately over the eligible tested features in each submitted request. Restricting markers changes this testing family, so adjusted p-values can differ from the frozen report even when individual effects and raw p-values agree. The app does not recalculate or replace the original report's adjustment family. These are exploratory comparisons of cells within one donor . Cells are not independent biological replicates, and the results do not establish an effect across donors. Selecting cells using the same markers or an embedding derived from them can introduce selection bias. Neither the donor restriction nor a small p-value resolves that problem. Missing scores and filtering Preparation retains observed cell–pair rows. Before a spatial test, both markers must pass the donor's pinned background-fraction threshold, and the score must be finite. A missing, filtered-out, or non-finite observation is never converted to zero. A measured score of zero remains an observation. The demo's threshold is computed from all prepared cells in that donor as max(median(isotype_fraction) + 2 * mad(isotype_fraction), 0.001) . It is fixed during preparation, not recomputed after lasso selection. Both demo donors have a cutoff of 0.001. The source pipeline's median/MAD settings are read from its stored report configuration. The current preparer supports this isotype mode without extra marker-count or pair-count filters; incompatible configurations are rejected instead of silently changed. Results distinguish n_cells_a/b (all selected cells) from n_scored_a/b (retained observations for this particular feature). Spatial eligibility uses the latter. Unsupported features have missing statistics and an explicit status. Stored spatial report profiles may use a different missing-observation summary convention; those means are never used to reconstruct new tests. Application bundle and sidecar schemas The version 2 application RDS is a plain R list, not a Seurat object: bundle_version = 2L ; contract retains the version 1 frozen-analysis contract, report settings, defaults, QC, and provenance. metadata and embeddings contain prepared cell annotations and coordinates. abundance and optional counts are aligned marker-by-cell sparse matrices. Counts are required for new abundance tests and proximity preparation. cell_sources , when present, maps component , original_id , and sample_id exactly from the original FSMap; IDs are never inferred by stripping prefixes. assets$proximity = list(path = "proximity", manifest = "manifest.rds") locates the proximity sidecar relative to the bundle directory. assets$graphs = list(path = "graphs", index = "index.rds") locates the optional node-only 3D sidecar. Proximity sidecar The proximity directory contains a version 1 manifest.rds and one Parquet partition per sample. Each row contains component , canonical marker_1 and marker_2 , log2_ratio , and min_marker_fraction (the smaller of the two marker counts divided by that cell's total count). Storing the minimum is equivalent to requiring both marker fractions to pass the same threshold. The manifest contains the dataset ID, a fingerprint of metadata, counts, cell-ID mapping and filter settings, donor cutoffs, row counts, partition MD5s, and source PXL paths/checksums. Preparation verifies source checksums against the frozen report inventory and checks that inputs did not change during extraction. PXL connections are read-only; SQL exports selected columns/cells directly to Parquet without collecting the full proximity table in R. The reader validates dataset identity, partition checksums, and paths within the bundle directory, then filters cells/markers before collecting at most the row limit plus one. File-system traversal and escaping symlinks are rejected. The worker also checks the load-time RDS checksum pinned to the user's request, so replacing an RDS under the same dataset ID cannot silently run a different analysis. RDS inputs and sidecars must still come from trusted preparation. Node-only 3D sidecar The graph directory contains one Parquet file per prepared sample and a small index.rds with schema_version = 3L . This graph-index version is separate from the application bundle version and the frozen-report contract version. Parquet contains exactly these columns: Column Contents cell_id Exact current cell ID in the application bundle x , y , z Finite prepared 3D graph-layout coordinates markers List of marker identities present at that node; no counts Source node IDs are used only during preparation to join marker identities and reject duplicate layout nodes, then discarded before writing Parquet. Hover shows marker identities; node CSV exports contain the same five columns above. Keep the source PXL for node-level traceability: exported rows no longer carry source node IDs. Existing version 2 Parquet files remain readable; Arrow excludes their node-ID column before loading, and the displayed asset uses version 3. All source layout nodes are retained, including nodes without a highlighted marker. No edges, marker-count matrices, dataset metadata, or repeated source provenance are stored in the Parquet rows. The index holds the dataset identity, prepared coverage, and two tables: Index table Columns cells cell_id , source_cell_id , sample , n_nodes samples sample , file , md5 , size_bytes , source_pxl , source_pxl_md5 , layout , graph_projection , n_nodes , n_cells The source cell mapping is checked against the bundle's exact FSMap-derived mapping. Source PXL checksums are checked against the frozen inventory when it is present, without opening the original PXL files. Source/layout provenance is stored once in the index and included in the selected cell's JSON export. The demo's observed source layout is coarsened_pmds_3d with graph_projection = "full" . This corrects the earlier wpmds_3d provenance label; preparation preserves the source coordinates rather than recomputing them. Runtime queries filter cell_id through Arrow before collecting nodes. Parquet row-group pruning avoids collecting the whole sample. The first access to a sample may read its entire file to validate the checksum; subsequent selections reuse checksum validation for the unchanged file. That initial disk scan is different from loading all sample nodes into R. The viewer rejects cells above 200,000 nodes instead of silently truncating them. Cell 3D uses CRAN threejs for rotation, zoom, hover, one highlight marker, and node/provenance downloads. It has no edge display. Highlights represent marker identities, not signal counts; shared-node highlights do not constitute a statistical colocalization test. Coordinates are abstract graph-layout positions, not physical microscopy positions or measured distances. The viewer keeps all nodes and uses one common coordinate scale, not separate axis stretching. Reset view restores the camera; Save PNG captures the canvas. Switching the highlight for the same cell preserves the camera, while changing cells resets it. Old WebGL resources are released on each Display. Plotly remains the renderer for embeddings and precomputed results. Download rotating GIF exports the displayed cell/highlight through one full turn around the current camera's up axis, without changing the visible camera. Expand Rotating GIF settings for duration (1–20 whole seconds), frame rate (1–30 FPS), and square image size (128–1024 pixels per side). Defaults are 6 seconds, 15 FPS, and 600 × 600 pixels. GIF frame delays have centisecond precision; rounding is distributed so the full animation retains its duration. The export has a white background and loops continuously. GIF's 256-color palette may slightly change the appearance of translucent points. Encoding runs in a browser worker using locally bundled gifenc 1.0.3 (MIT; license in www/vendor/gifenc-LICENSE.txt ), with one captured frame in flight at a time. No external CDN, PXL read, server-side analysis, or new R dependency is needed. Progress and Cancel GIF remain available; Display is disabled until the export ends. Replacing/unbinding the graph cancels its export. Limits of 300 frames, 120 million total pixels, and 64 MiB encoded output bound work and memory; reduce duration, FPS, or image size if a limit is reached. Choose donor, cell type, condition, and two ranking markers (the same marker twice for a self-pair). Reversed pair orders are equivalent. Ranking uses finite observed log2 ratios, descending with cell-ID tie breaking; it does not apply abundance/differential-test cutoffs or replace missing scores with zero. A progress indicator appears while ranking. Choose top 10, bottom 10, their deduplicated union, or all scored cells; download the current ranking as CSV. Cells without prepared graphs are identified in the list. Clear both ranking markers to browse prepared cells without ranking. Select one highlight marker and click Display to load the selected cell. Changing filters, ranking, cell, or highlight does not redraw the last displayed graph. Node and provenance downloads refer to that displayed snapshot. Preparation can target selected cells. A later invocation retains the union of previously prepared and newly requested cells, atomically rewrites affected sample files, and updates the index. Unaffected, validated sample files are reused. Run preparers sequentially against a given directory. Version 1 per-cell RDS graph indexes are rejected with a rebuild instruction: preserve the old directory and prepare version 3 assets in a new one. Version 2 sample Parquet sidecars are read-only: rebuild in a new directory to remove their stored node IDs. The preparer does not perform an automatic destructive migration or mix schema versions within one graph directory. Dependencies and preparation Install the CRAN renderer with install.packages("threejs") (version >= 0.3.4). The plain-bundle viewer uses the packages in DESCRIPTION 's Imports ; it does not require Seurat/PNA class definitions merely to load data. Legacy Seurat RDS inputs still require SeuratObject, and PNA inputs require pixelatorR. Background differential analysis requires pixelatorR, Seurat, and SeuratObject; spatial querying additionally requires Arrow and dplyr. Cell 3D also requires Arrow and dplyr in the Shiny R environment, but not Seurat or pixelatorR for a plain bundle. Offline graph preparation requires the source Seurat/PNA object, pixelatorR, Arrow, and dplyr; PXL-to-Parquet preparation also uses DBI and DuckDB. Neither the analysis worker nor the 3D viewer needs PXL mounts or permission to access the original files. Renderer comparison (2026-10-12) The saved measurements are in docs/benchmarks/2026-10-12-cell-renderers/ : R timings and sizes (CSV) , browser measurements (JSON) , and test cases and package versions (JSON) . These are unchanged copies of the measured results, including the optional OrbitControls comparison. The file fields name generated HTML snapshots in output/renderer-benchmark , not files included in this small results archive. Compared CRAN threejs 0.3.4 with the existing Plotly 4.12.1 renderer from commit bb341b2 , using three real demo cells, all nodes, the same CD44 highlight, marker hover labels, preserved aspect ratios, and 1000 × 700 widgets. The cells are the smallest, median, and largest among those within the unchanged 200,000-node limit. Nodes Plotly browser ready threejs browser ready Plotly / threejs HTML payload 10,021 1,165 ms 159 ms 1.65 / 0.88 MB 41,111 1,636 ms 347 ms 6.66 / 3.48 MB 197,680 5,439 ms 713 ms 32.29 / 16.92 MB These are observations from one controlled browser pass, not end-to-end Shiny latency or hardware-GPU guarantees. Browser-ready time is navigation to two animation frames after the htmlwidget render hook. Each case ran in a fresh Chrome 149.0.7827.55 process, after warming dependencies on the smallest cell, with back/forward caching disabled. The server has no available hardware WebGL: the test used SwiftShader with four workers, CPU affinity 0–3, single-threaded V8, and device scale 1. Shared-library download sizes are excluded from the HTML payload; MB here means decimal megabytes. During a two-second mouse drag, animation-frame callback rates were approximately 5.8 / 60.0, 2.0 / 27.8, and 0.5 / 7.8 Hz (Plotly / threejs). This measures browser responsiveness, not an independent GPU frame counter. The post-GC JavaScript heap was 10.8 / 4.2, 17.4 / 9.0, and 51.7 / 33.7 MiB; it excludes native/GPU memory. The alternative threejs OrbitControls were also tested; the app retains the default TrackballControls for unrestricted rotation. The app disables residual camera inertia so Reset stays at the initial view, and wakes rendering for idle zoom events; these small interaction fixes are not part of the renderer benchmark. R construction is not uniformly faster: medians of three warmed builds were 146 / 134, 560 / 592, and 2,687 / 3,097 ms. The largest threejs R widget was also larger (15.85 versus 14.31 MB). The switch therefore targets browser responsiveness and the roughly 47% smaller serialized plot payload, not R-side memory savings. No downsampling, sidecar schema change, or node-limit increase was used. To reproduce, run Rscript scripts/benchmark_cell_renderers.R from the repository root with the demo sidecars and CRAN threejs installed. Serve output/renderer-benchmark locally on port 3840, then run PROXIOME_CHROME=/path/to/chromium PROXIOME_BENCH_CPUS=0-3 node tests/browser_renderer_benchmark.mjs . docs.text: The application separates three operations: viewing frozen results, submitting a bounded new comparison to an R worker, and opening prepared cell graphs. Viewing or filtering a report never changes its stored statistics. Runtime analysis reads a prepared proximity sidecar, not PXL files.

docs.text: Open the exploratory-analysis tab, choose one donor, one cell type, two distinct conditions, a readout, and the markers to test. Use all cells in that scope, or select a subset using the embedding's lasso/box tools or the cell selector. The selected conditions assign cells to target and reference groups; cells cannot belong to both. The displayed counts update before submission. Confirm the exploratory-analysis notice and click Run comparison . An R process performs the test while the reports remain usable. Changing controls does not rerun a test. The result identifies the submitted scope; downloads include the results CSV and JSON provenance with the exact selected cell IDs. The volcano supports hover, box/scroll zoom, and double-click reset. The results table also includes requested features that could not be tested. Only one background analysis runs at a time per application process. The server limits each request to 2,000 cells, 160 markers, 1,000 unordered non-self pairs, and 1,000,000 retained score rows, with a 120-second timeout. Colocalization tests all combinations of the chosen markers: 45 markers produce 990 pairs; 46 exceed the cap. Oversized selections are rejected, not silently downsampled. Cancel a running job or narrow the cells/markers if it exceeds a limit.
docs.title: Running a new comparison

docs.text: Readout Effect: target minus reference Test and minimum support Abundance Mean stored normalized abundance pixelatorR::RunDAA , using Seurat's two-sided Wilcoxon test; at least 3 selected cells per group Self-proximity Median observed log2_ratio for each marker paired with itself pixelatorR::DifferentialProximityAnalysis(metric_type = "self") ; at least 20 retained observations per marker in each group Colocalization Median observed log2_ratio for each unordered pair of different markers pixelatorR::DifferentialProximityAnalysis(metric_type = "co") ; at least 40 retained observations per pair in each group Abundance uses the bundle's existing transformed layer without renormalization: mean_fxn = Matrix::rowMeans , fc_name = "difference" , slot = fc.slot = "data" on a temporary assay containing those stored values, min.pct = 0 , test.use = "wilcox" . RunDAA sets logfc.threshold = 0 and applies BH correction to the returned marker p-values. The demo layer contains CLR abundance. Three cells is the API's testing minimum, not evidence that a small comparison is well powered; the original pipeline recommends 20 for abundance. Spatial tests use the package's two-sided, tie-corrected rank test with continuity correction. The effect is a difference of median log2 ratios , not the log fold-change in mean abundance. The preparation formula is log2(pmax(join_count, 1) / pmax(join_count_expected_mean, 1)) . BH adjustment is performed separately over the eligible tested features in each submitted request. Restricting markers changes this testing family, so adjusted p-values can differ from the frozen report even when individual effects and raw p-values agree. The app does not recalculate or replace the original report's adjustment family. These are exploratory comparisons of cells within one donor . Cells are not independent biological replicates, and the results do not establish an effect across donors. Selecting cells using the same markers or an embedding derived from them can introduce selection bias. Neither the donor restriction nor a small p-value resolves that problem.
docs.title: Methods and interpretation

docs.text: Preparation retains observed cell–pair rows. Before a spatial test, both markers must pass the donor's pinned background-fraction threshold, and the score must be finite. A missing, filtered-out, or non-finite observation is never converted to zero. A measured score of zero remains an observation. The demo's threshold is computed from all prepared cells in that donor as max(median(isotype_fraction) + 2 * mad(isotype_fraction), 0.001) . It is fixed during preparation, not recomputed after lasso selection. Both demo donors have a cutoff of 0.001. The source pipeline's median/MAD settings are read from its stored report configuration. The current preparer supports this isotype mode without extra marker-count or pair-count filters; incompatible configurations are rejected instead of silently changed. Results distinguish n_cells_a/b (all selected cells) from n_scored_a/b (retained observations for this particular feature). Spatial eligibility uses the latter. Unsupported features have missing statistics and an explicit status. Stored spatial report profiles may use a different missing-observation summary convention; those means are never used to reconstruct new tests.

docs.text: The version 2 application RDS is a plain R list, not a Seurat object: bundle_version = 2L ; contract retains the version 1 frozen-analysis contract, report settings, defaults, QC, and provenance. metadata and embeddings contain prepared cell annotations and coordinates. abundance and optional counts are aligned marker-by-cell sparse matrices. Counts are required for new abundance tests and proximity preparation. cell_sources , when present, maps component , original_id , and sample_id exactly from the original FSMap; IDs are never inferred by stripping prefixes. assets$proximity = list(path = "proximity", manifest = "manifest.rds") locates the proximity sidecar relative to the bundle directory. assets$graphs = list(path = "graphs", index = "index.rds") locates the optional node-only 3D sidecar.

docs.text: The proximity directory contains a version 1 manifest.rds and one Parquet partition per sample. Each row contains component , canonical marker_1 and marker_2 , log2_ratio , and min_marker_fraction (the smaller of the two marker counts divided by that cell's total count). Storing the minimum is equivalent to requiring both marker fractions to pass the same threshold. The manifest contains the dataset ID, a fingerprint of metadata, counts, cell-ID mapping and filter settings, donor cutoffs, row counts, partition MD5s, and source PXL paths/checksums. Preparation verifies source checksums against the frozen report inventory and checks that inputs did not change during extraction. PXL connections are read-only; SQL exports selected columns/cells directly to Parquet without collecting the full proximity table in R. The reader validates dataset identity, partition checksums, and paths within the bundle directory, then filters cells/markers before collecting at most the row limit plus one. File-system traversal and escaping symlinks are rejected. The worker also checks the load-time RDS checksum pinned to the user's request, so replacing an RDS under the same dataset ID cannot silently run a different analysis. RDS inputs and sidecars must still come from trusted preparation.

docs.text: The graph directory contains one Parquet file per prepared sample and a small index.rds with schema_version = 3L . This graph-index version is separate from the application bundle version and the frozen-report contract version. Parquet contains exactly these columns: Column Contents cell_id Exact current cell ID in the application bundle x , y , z Finite prepared 3D graph-layout coordinates markers List of marker identities present at that node; no counts Source node IDs are used only during preparation to join marker identities and reject duplicate layout nodes, then discarded before writing Parquet. Hover shows marker identities; node CSV exports contain the same five columns above. Keep the source PXL for node-level traceability: exported rows no longer carry source node IDs. Existing version 2 Parquet files remain readable; Arrow excludes their node-ID column before loading, and the displayed asset uses version 3. All source layout nodes are retained, including nodes without a highlighted marker. No edges, marker-count matrices, dataset metadata, or repeated source provenance are stored in the Parquet rows. The index holds the dataset identity, prepared coverage, and two tables: Index table Columns cells cell_id , source_cell_id , sample , n_nodes samples sample , file , md5 , size_bytes , source_pxl , source_pxl_md5 , layout , graph_projection , n_nodes , n_cells The source cell mapping is checked against the bundle's exact FSMap-derived mapping. Source PXL checksums are checked against the frozen inventory when it is present, without opening the original PXL files. Source/layout provenance is stored once in the index and included in the selected cell's JSON export. The demo's observed source layout is coarsened_pmds_3d with graph_projection = "full" . This corrects the earlier wpmds_3d provenance label; preparation preserves the source coordinates rather than recomputing them. Runtime queries filter cell_id through Arrow before collecting nodes. Parquet row-group pruning avoids collecting the whole sample. The first access to a sample may read its entire file to validate the checksum; subsequent selections reuse checksum validation for the unchanged file. That initial disk scan is different from loading all sample nodes into R. The viewer rejects cells above 200,000 nodes instead of silently truncating them. Cell 3D uses CRAN threejs for rotation, zoom, hover, one highlight marker, and node/provenance downloads. It has no edge display. Highlights represent marker identities, not signal counts; shared-node highlights do not constitute a statistical colocalization test. Coordinates are abstract graph-layout positions, not physical microscopy positions or measured distances. The viewer keeps all nodes and uses one common coordinate scale, not separate axis stretching. Reset view restores the camera; Save PNG captures the canvas. Switching the highlight for the same cell preserves the camera, while changing cells resets it. Old WebGL resources are released on each Display. Plotly remains the renderer for embeddings and precomputed results. Download rotating GIF exports the displayed cell/highlight through one full turn around the current camera's up axis, without changing the visible camera. Expand Rotating GIF settings for duration (1–20 whole seconds), frame rate (1–30 FPS), and square image size (128–1024 pixels per side). Defaults are 6 seconds, 15 FPS, and 600 × 600 pixels. GIF frame delays have centisecond precision; rounding is distributed so the full animation retains its duration. The export has a white background and loops continuously. GIF's 256-color palette may slightly change the appearance of translucent points. Encoding runs in a browser worker using locally bundled gifenc 1.0.3 (MIT; license in www/vendor/gifenc-LICENSE.txt ), with one captured frame in flight at a time. No external CDN, PXL read, server-side analysis, or new R dependency is needed. Progress and Cancel GIF remain available; Display is disabled until the export ends. Replacing/unbinding the graph cancels its export. Limits of 300 frames, 120 million total pixels, and 64 MiB encoded output bound work and memory; reduce duration, FPS, or image size if a limit is reached. Choose donor, cell type, condition, and two ranking markers (the same marker twice for a self-pair). Reversed pair orders are equivalent. Ranking uses finite observed log2 ratios, descending with cell-ID tie breaking; it does not apply abundance/differential-test cutoffs or replace missing scores with zero. A progress indicator appears while ranking. Choose top 10, bottom 10, their deduplicated union, or all scored cells; download the current ranking as CSV. Cells without prepared graphs are identified in the list. Clear both ranking markers to browse prepared cells without ranking. Select one highlight marker and click Display to load the selected cell. Changing filters, ranking, cell, or highlight does not redraw the last displayed graph. Node and provenance downloads refer to that displayed snapshot. Preparation can target selected cells. A later invocation retains the union of previously prepared and newly requested cells, atomically rewrites affected sample files, and updates the index. Unaffected, validated sample files are reused. Run preparers sequentially against a given directory. Version 1 per-cell RDS graph indexes are rejected with a rebuild instruction: preserve the old directory and prepare version 3 assets in a new one. Version 2 sample Parquet sidecars are read-only: rebuild in a new directory to remove their stored node IDs. The preparer does not perform an automatic destructive migration or mix schema versions within one graph directory.

docs.text: Precomputed results The report views consume a versioned frozen-analysis contract. The recommended application file is a compact plain-R bundle; legacy Seurat RDS files remain supported. Filtering a report never changes its stored statistics. The separate Custom analysis tab can submit a new bounded comparison to an R worker using prepared cell-level inputs; see Hybrid analysis . Prepare the frozen results Run the builder once after the upstream analysis has completed: Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_precomputed_rds.R \ ../pixelgen_demo_data/demo_analysis/cca_analysis/results/demo_cca_clustered.rds \ ../pixelgen_demo_data/demo_analysis/tertiary_analysis \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds The arguments are: INPUT_RDS : the annotated Seurat object used by the analysis. ANALYSIS_DIR : the analysis directory containing the frozen result tables. OUTPUT_RDS : the legacy frozen-results Seurat RDS; normally output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds . The output/ directory is gitignored. Build or deliver the RDS separately on the deployment host rather than committing it with the application source. The input object must contain cell metadata that can be mapped to these fields: Field Meaning component Current cell/component identifier sample_id Experimental sample identifier donor Biological donor identifier condition Experimental condition celltype Cell-type annotation cluster Stored cluster annotation The builder validates its inputs and writes a separate output file. It does not modify the input RDS or anything below the ../pixelgen_demo_data source tree. This builder is intentionally specific to the demo directory layout and its d1 / d2 donor outputs; the versioned application contract is the reusable boundary for other preparation pipelines. Export a plain application bundle To view frozen results without Seurat/PNA classes on the deployment host, export the prepared file in the analysis environment: Rscript --vanilla -e 'source("R/precomputed_contract.R"); write_precomputed_bundle(read_precomputed_rds("output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds"), "output/proxiomevis_app_v2.rds")' Set PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS to the exported file when starting Shiny. This export needs no PXL access and does not add spatial or graph sidecars. Its sparse counts and stored abundance can support new abundance tests when the worker dependencies are installed. For the complete demo bundle, including proximity and cell-graph sidecars, run: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ARROW_NUM_THREADS=1 \ Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds output/hybrid_demo This preparation needs the source PXL files. The optional third argument is their directory if they moved. The deployed output contains analysis.rds , proximity/ , and graphs/ ; keep the relative directory layout intact. Full graph preparation can be lengthy and is resumable, but do not run two preparers in the same output directory. The graph sidecar is one node-only Parquet file per prepared sample plus a version 3 index, not per-cell RDS files. Source and layout provenance belong in that index; Parquet rows contain only cell IDs, coordinates, and marker identities. Version 2 remains readable without loading node IDs. Rebuild older graph exports in a new directory to obtain version 3; do not change their version field by hand. See Getting started for startup and Hybrid analysis for sidecar schemas and dependencies. The plain R list has these fields: Field Contents bundle_version 2L , the application file format version contract The unchanged frozen contract with schema_version = 1L metadata , embeddings Prepared cell metadata and all stored reductions abundance Aligned sparse marker-by-cell transformed abundance counts Optional aligned sparse counts; needed for new abundance tests and proximity preparation cell_sources Optional exact component , original_id , and sample_id mapping from FSMap assets Optional relative descriptors for proximity and graph sidecars No Seurat/PNA object, per-cell proximity table, or 3D node table is included in this application bundle. The reader adds bundle_path and a load-time bundle_md5 in memory; these are runtime identity fields and are not exported into the RDS. Frozen analysis contract The first builder's output remains a Seurat object, with its contract at: object@misc$proxiomevis In the plain bundle the same contract is stored at bundle$contract . Its version 1 fields contain: schema_version integer contract version dataset_id, title stable identifier and display title defaults reduction, metadata-column, assay, and layer mappings sample_summaries one stored value per sample and feature donor_contrasts stored group A minus group B effect for each donor differential_results descriptive effects combined across donors qc frozen cell-count table provenance source and preparation details report frozen source rows and settings used by report plots proximity_source optional source-PXL locations for offline preparation Each of the three result sections must contain these named readouts: abundance stores marker abundance summaries and contrasts. self_proximity stores marker self-proximity, where the two marker fields are identical. colocalization stores proximity between two different markers. All readout tables identify the cell type, feature, ordered marker pair, metric, and control-marker status. Sample summaries additionally retain the sample, donor, condition, value, and total/evaluable/scored cell counts. Donor contrasts retain the analysis ID, comparison labels, donor, source effect, cell counts, and original exploratory test fields. Differential results retain the effect range, donor-pair count, direction agreement, method, replicate unit, inference label, and multiple-testing fields. Abundance sample values use mean_clr , and abundance contrasts use delta_mean_clr ; their frozen group means are stored in value_a and value_b . Spatial sample values use the source population mean log2_ratio with the original missing-as-zero policy. Spatial effects use the original difference of observed medians ( delta_median_log2_ratio ). Because those two source group medians were not persisted, spatial value_a and value_b are NA ; effect_size is the authoritative stored effect and must not be inferred from the sample-profile means. For this two-donor dataset, the combined differential_results rows are descriptive and their p_value and p_adj fields must be NA . The contract validator rejects a descriptive row carrying inferential probabilities. The optional report bundle is deliberately separate. It retains the original donor-specific tertiary outputs needed to reproduce the established figures: source result rows, eligibility tables, spatial profiles, resolved settings, the cross-donor alignment bundle, and frozen abundance heatmap matrices. Those source result rows can contain the tertiary analysis's component-level p / p_adj values. The app displays them unchanged as exploratory component-level tests; it does not reinterpret them as donor-level inference or combine them into a new test. In a legacy input, the Seurat object supplies per-cell metadata, embeddings, and abundance values. The plain bundle stores those extracted values directly. defaults retains the prepared reductions, metadata mappings, assay name, and abundance-layer identity: reduction, pca_reduction celltype_column, cluster_column, donor_column, condition_column, sample_column assay, abundance_layer The reductions must contain finite coordinates aligned to the cells. A legacy input's configured assay must contain counts and the configured abundance layer, and its cell-level proximity slots must be empty. Plain bundles validate the extracted matrices and metadata without constructing a Seurat assay. Large per-cell proximity tables belong in optional disk-backed sidecars, not the RDS. Consumers should validate the contract version and required columns before rendering any view. A newer incompatible layout should use a new version rather than silently changing the meaning of an existing field. Explore one donor's stored results The top navigation groups stored views under Precomputed results . Its shared selection bar contains donor, cell type, comparison, and readout. A single-donor dataset displays the donor as a fixed label; multi-donor datasets offer a donor dropdown, but every result view still uses one donor's original stored contrast. The descriptive cross-donor rows remain preserved in the contract; they are not required or substituted for donor-specific effects by this interface. The four subtabs are: Subtab Contents Summary Differential effects for the selected cell type, or across all cell types; optional original abundance heatmap Volcano One donor and one cell type's original stored test with hover, zoom, and feature selection Spatial matrix Aligned self-proximity and colocalization, either condition profiles or differential effects Tables & methods Searchable result and volcano rows, sample support, exports, and method settings Choosing All cell types (summary) is supported by the heatmap and tables. Volcano and spatial views then ask for one cell type rather than silently choosing a different scope. Comparison labels retain target/reference direction: a positive effect means target exceeds reference. Results come from stored rows; these controls do not reopen PXL, recalculate proximity, rerun eligibility filters, or fit a new test. Click a heatmap tile, volcano point, spatial marker pair, or result-table row to select the same feature in the detail panel shared by all four views. Pair keys are order-independent. The panel shows the selected scope's stored effect, available probabilities, and cell support; condition values are shown only if present in the contract. A feature without a stored test is labeled as such instead of being converted to a zero effect. Explore cells in 3D transfers that donor, cell type, and pair. The user must choose a condition from the comparison and one highlight marker, then click Display . The handoff does not load a graph or alter the previously displayed 3D view. It can initiate ranking only after a condition is chosen and the required proximity sidecar is available. Statistical meaning and spatial exploration Original donor-specific volcanoes may display the stored component-level P values described above. These are exploratory within-donor tests, not evidence of a population-level treatment effect. Cells from one donor are not independent biological replicates. The same limitation applies to a dataset containing only one donor; no combined or pooled test is invented. The spatial matrix deliberately combines self-proximity and colocalization, independent of the readout control used by the other subtabs. Hover exposes the pair, stored value, and availability; click selects the pair for detail. The marker order and aligned scales follow the frozen report. Condition profiles show stored population means with the upstream missing-as-zero policy, while differential effects show differences of observed medians. The former must not be subtracted to reconstruct the latter. Untested or unavailable entries are distinguished from measured values near zero. Custom analysis instead submits an explicit selected-cell comparison to a background R process with its own result and provenance. Those new P values remain exploratory, and selection using the same data can bias testing. Filters, exports, and rendering FDR controls are labeled table filters; the app does not apply them to the original report plots. When no adjusted P values were stored, these controls are unavailable rather than fabricated. Table searches and FDR filters affect the corresponding Filtered table CSV , including all matching rows rather than just the current page. All stored rows CSV ignores both filters and exports the selected donor/cell-type/comparison/readout scope. Heatmap feature counts and control-marker display options affect only the summary display. Original report SVG preserves the upstream report plotting strategy and thresholds. The interactive spatial view also offers its displayed rows as CSV. The methods section exposes stored effect metrics, original settings, test methods, and multiple-testing information where available; it does not infer missing method details. Plot outputs are suspended while their subtab is hidden; shared selections and the selected feature persist while navigating. Prepared views read only the loaded RDS. Sidecars are used for explicit cell-level ranking, graph display, or custom spatial analysis, not merely for viewing a stored result. Runtime and PXL files Both supported RDS formats contain all three frozen readouts, so those views need no mounted PXL file. New spatial tests require the prepared proximity sidecar; Cell 3D requires prepared graph assets. These runtime features also need no PXL access. Missing sidecars do not prevent frozen report viewing. Cell 3D additionally requires Arrow and dplyr to select nodes from its sample's Parquet file. Graph data is not collected for all cells when opening the RDS. Only offline preparation needs the original PXL files. Plain-bundle loading requires Matrix but not Seurat or pixelatorR. Legacy Seurat inputs still require SeuratObject, and PNA inputs require pixelatorR's class definitions. The read_precomputed_rds() helper handles supported input formats; background testing has additional package requirements documented in Hybrid analysis . Security RDS is an R serialization format, not a safe public upload format. Only load files produced by a trusted analysis pipeline. Prefer an administrator-managed server directory and PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS ; do not accept arbitrary internet uploads and pass them to readRDS() . The optional PROXIOME_ALLOW_LOCAL_LOAD=true flag exposes a server-path field for a trusted local operator. Leave it unset on public deployments because it allows the visitor to select any readable server-side RDS path.

For the complete demo bundle, including proximity and cell-graph sidecars, run: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ARROW_NUM_THREADS=1 \ Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds output/hybrid_demo This preparation needs the source PXL files. The optional third argument is their directory if they moved. The deployed output contains analysis.rds , proximity/ , and graphs/ ; keep the relative directory layout intact. Full graph preparation can be lengthy and is resumable, but do not run two preparers in the same output directory. The graph sidecar is one node-only Parquet file per prepared sample plus a version 3 index, not per-cell RDS files. Source and layout provenance belong in that index; Parquet rows contain only cell IDs, coordinates, and marker identities. Version 2 remains readable without loading node IDs. Rebuild older graph exports in a new directory to obtain version 3; do not change their version field by hand. See Getting started for startup and Hybrid analysis for sidecar schemas and dependencies. The plain R list has these fields: Field Contents bundle_version 2L , the application file format version contract The unchanged frozen contract with schema_version = 1L metadata , embeddings Prepared cell metadata and all stored reductions abundance Aligned sparse marker-by-cell transformed abundance counts Optional aligned sparse counts; needed for new abundance tests and proximity preparation cell_sources Optional exact component , original_id , and sample_id mapping from FSMap assets Optional relative descriptors for proximity and graph sidecars No Seurat/PNA object, per-cell proximity table, or 3D node table is included in this application bundle. The reader adds bundle_path and a load-time bundle_md5 in memory; these are runtime identity fields and are not exported into the RDS.

docs.text: The first builder's output remains a Seurat object, with its contract at: object@misc$proxiomevis In the plain bundle the same contract is stored at bundle$contract . Its version 1 fields contain: schema_version integer contract version dataset_id, title stable identifier and display title defaults reduction, metadata-column, assay, and layer mappings sample_summaries one stored value per sample and feature donor_contrasts stored group A minus group B effect for each donor differential_results descriptive effects combined across donors qc frozen cell-count table provenance source and preparation details report frozen source rows and settings used by report plots proximity_source optional source-PXL locations for offline preparation Each of the three result sections must contain these named readouts: abundance stores marker abundance summaries and contrasts. self_proximity stores marker self-proximity, where the two marker fields are identical. colocalization stores proximity between two different markers. All readout tables identify the cell type, feature, ordered marker pair, metric, and control-marker status. Sample summaries additionally retain the sample, donor, condition, value, and total/evaluable/scored cell counts. Donor contrasts retain the analysis ID, comparison labels, donor, source effect, cell counts, and original exploratory test fields. Differential results retain the effect range, donor-pair count, direction agreement, method, replicate unit, inference label, and multiple-testing fields. Abundance sample values use mean_clr , and abundance contrasts use delta_mean_clr ; their frozen group means are stored in value_a and value_b . Spatial sample values use the source population mean log2_ratio with the original missing-as-zero policy. Spatial effects use the original difference of observed medians ( delta_median_log2_ratio ). Because those two source group medians were not persisted, spatial value_a and value_b are NA ; effect_size is the authoritative stored effect and must not be inferred from the sample-profile means. For this two-donor dataset, the combined differential_results rows are descriptive and their p_value and p_adj fields must be NA . The contract validator rejects a descriptive row carrying inferential probabilities. The optional report bundle is deliberately separate. It retains the original donor-specific tertiary outputs needed to reproduce the established figures: source result rows, eligibility tables, spatial profiles, resolved settings, the cross-donor alignment bundle, and frozen abundance heatmap matrices. Those source result rows can contain the tertiary analysis's component-level p / p_adj values. The app displays them unchanged as exploratory component-level tests; it does not reinterpret them as donor-level inference or combine them into a new test. In a legacy input, the Seurat object supplies per-cell metadata, embeddings, and abundance values. The plain bundle stores those extracted values directly. defaults retains the prepared reductions, metadata mappings, assay name, and abundance-layer identity: reduction, pca_reduction celltype_column, cluster_column, donor_column, condition_column, sample_column assay, abundance_layer The reductions must contain finite coordinates aligned to the cells. A legacy input's configured assay must contain counts and the configured abundance layer, and its cell-level proximity slots must be empty. Plain bundles validate the extracted matrices and metadata without constructing a Seurat assay. Large per-cell proximity tables belong in optional disk-backed sidecars, not the RDS. Consumers should validate the contract version and required columns before rendering any view. A newer incompatible layout should use a new version rather than silently changing the meaning of an existing field.
docs.title: Frozen analysis contract

docs.text: The top navigation groups stored views under Precomputed results . Its shared selection bar contains donor, cell type, comparison, and readout. A single-donor dataset displays the donor as a fixed label; multi-donor datasets offer a donor dropdown, but every result view still uses one donor's original stored contrast. The descriptive cross-donor rows remain preserved in the contract; they are not required or substituted for donor-specific effects by this interface. The four subtabs are: Subtab Contents Summary Differential effects for the selected cell type, or across all cell types; optional original abundance heatmap Volcano One donor and one cell type's original stored test with hover, zoom, and feature selection Spatial matrix Aligned self-proximity and colocalization, either condition profiles or differential effects Tables & methods Searchable result and volcano rows, sample support, exports, and method settings Choosing All cell types (summary) is supported by the heatmap and tables. Volcano and spatial views then ask for one cell type rather than silently choosing a different scope. Comparison labels retain target/reference direction: a positive effect means target exceeds reference. Results come from stored rows; these controls do not reopen PXL, recalculate proximity, rerun eligibility filters, or fit a new test. Click a heatmap tile, volcano point, spatial marker pair, or result-table row to select the same feature in the detail panel shared by all four views. Pair keys are order-independent. The panel shows the selected scope's stored effect, available probabilities, and cell support; condition values are shown only if present in the contract. A feature without a stored test is labeled as such instead of being converted to a zero effect. Explore cells in 3D transfers that donor, cell type, and pair. The user must choose a condition from the comparison and one highlight marker, then click Display . The handoff does not load a graph or alter the previously displayed 3D view. It can initiate ranking only after a condition is chosen and the required proximity sidecar is available.
docs.title: Explore one donor's stored results

docs.text: Original donor-specific volcanoes may display the stored component-level P values described above. These are exploratory within-donor tests, not evidence of a population-level treatment effect. Cells from one donor are not independent biological replicates. The same limitation applies to a dataset containing only one donor; no combined or pooled test is invented. The spatial matrix deliberately combines self-proximity and colocalization, independent of the readout control used by the other subtabs. Hover exposes the pair, stored value, and availability; click selects the pair for detail. The marker order and aligned scales follow the frozen report. Condition profiles show stored population means with the upstream missing-as-zero policy, while differential effects show differences of observed medians. The former must not be subtracted to reconstruct the latter. Untested or unavailable entries are distinguished from measured values near zero. Custom analysis instead submits an explicit selected-cell comparison to a background R process with its own result and provenance. Those new P values remain exploratory, and selection using the same data can bias testing.
docs.title: Statistical meaning and spatial exploration

docs.text: FDR controls are labeled table filters; the app does not apply them to the original report plots. When no adjusted P values were stored, these controls are unavailable rather than fabricated. Table searches and FDR filters affect the corresponding Filtered table CSV , including all matching rows rather than just the current page. All stored rows CSV ignores both filters and exports the selected donor/cell-type/comparison/readout scope. Heatmap feature counts and control-marker display options affect only the summary display. Original report SVG preserves the upstream report plotting strategy and thresholds. The interactive spatial view also offers its displayed rows as CSV. The methods section exposes stored effect metrics, original settings, test methods, and multiple-testing information where available; it does not infer missing method details. Plot outputs are suspended while their subtab is hidden; shared selections and the selected feature persist while navigating. Prepared views read only the loaded RDS. Sidecars are used for explicit cell-level ranking, graph display, or custom spatial analysis, not merely for viewing a stored result.
docs.title: Filters, exports, and rendering

docs.text: Both supported RDS formats contain all three frozen readouts, so those views need no mounted PXL file. New spatial tests require the prepared proximity sidecar; Cell 3D requires prepared graph assets. These runtime features also need no PXL access. Missing sidecars do not prevent frozen report viewing. Cell 3D additionally requires Arrow and dplyr to select nodes from its sample's Parquet file. Graph data is not collected for all cells when opening the RDS. Only offline preparation needs the original PXL files. Plain-bundle loading requires Matrix but not Seurat or pixelatorR. Legacy Seurat inputs still require SeuratObject, and PNA inputs require pixelatorR's class definitions. The read_precomputed_rds() helper handles supported input formats; background testing has additional package requirements documented in Hybrid analysis .
docs.title: Runtime and PXL files

docs.text: RDS is an R serialization format, not a safe public upload format. Only load files produced by a trusted analysis pipeline. Prefer an administrator-managed server directory and PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS ; do not accept arbitrary internet uploads and pass them to readRDS() . The optional PROXIOME_ALLOW_LOCAL_LOAD=true flag exposes a server-path field for a trusted local operator. Leave it unset on public deployments because it allows the visitor to select any readable server-side RDS path.
docs.title: Security

docs.text: Troubleshooting The app cannot find its RDS The default is output/hybrid_demo/analysis.rds when present, otherwise output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds . Follow Getting started to prepare these, or set PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS to an absolute path readable by the Shiny process. The configured file must exist and end in .rds . The RDS fails contract validation The app accepts a plain application bundle with bundle_version = 2L or a legacy Seurat RDS. Both retain the frozen contract's schema_version = 1L ; these version numbers describe different structures and should not be changed to make an incompatible file load. Validation checks metadata mappings, coordinates, matrix/cell alignment, result-table columns, marker pairs, support counts, and descriptive-inference rules. Legacy inputs additionally need their configured assay layers and empty cell-level proximity slots. Rebuild the frozen demo contract with scripts/prepare_precomputed_rds.R , then export a plain bundle as described in Precomputed results . Do not patch invalid results merely to bypass validation. R reports an unknown PNA class This applies to legacy analysis files, not plain application bundles. Install SeuratObject and a pixelatorR version compatible with the source analysis in the R environment that runs the app, or export a plain bundle in the analysis environment and deploy that instead. Plain bundles need no Seurat/PNA classes for viewing; they still need the viewer packages in DESCRIPTION . Check which R executable starts Shiny if packages appear installed but cannot be found. This workspace's project environment is ../.pixi/envs/r/bin/Rscript ; it can differ from the system Rscript . A filter produces no rows Report controls only narrow the frozen tertiary results. Choose a donor, comparison, cell type, and feature present in those tables. A missing stored combination is not computed automatically. To run a new comparison, use Custom analysis and explicitly submit a valid cell selection. Its result is separate from the report and requires the appropriate cell-level inputs and worker dependencies. PXL files are unavailable PXL files are preparation inputs, not runtime requirements. Report views use the RDS, spatial tests use the prepared proximity sidecar, and Cell 3D loads the chosen cell's nodes from its sample's prepared Parquet file. If preparation itself fails because PXL paths moved, pass their directory as the third argument to scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R . Spatial analysis or Cell 3D says assets are missing A report-only RDS does not contain the optional sidecars. Prepare them upstream, then deploy analysis.rds together with its proximity/ and graphs/ directories. Asset descriptors are relative to the bundle directory; absolute paths, traversal, and symlinks escaping that directory are rejected. Graph coverage is shown explicitly. If preparation is still running, click Refresh prepared cells to see newly completed cells. Rerun the preparation command after an interruption to reuse validated completed sample files. Adding cells atomically rewrites affected files with the union of old and new cells; it does not remove previously prepared cells from coverage. Do not run two preparers concurrently in the same output directory. A failed partial proximity export without a manifest needs a fresh output directory; the standalone proximity preparer refuses to overwrite a nonempty directory. Cell 3D reports an unsupported graph index The current graph sidecar uses schema_version = 3L : one node-only Parquet file per sample plus index.rds , with no stored node IDs. Version 2 sample Parquet sidecars remain readable but cannot be extended by the preparer; rebuild in a new directory to get smaller version 3 files. Old version 1 per-cell RDS assets are not compatible. Do not change the version field by hand or delete the old directory to bypass the check. Preserve it and run scripts/prepare_hybrid_bundle.R with a new output directory, then deploy the new bundle and its sidecars together. There is no automatic destructive migration. Cell 3D is missing Arrow/dplyr or is slow on first load Install arrow and dplyr in the R environment running Shiny. Frozen reports still work without these optional graph-query dependencies. No pixelatorR or source PXL access is needed for viewing a plain bundle's prepared nodes. The first selection from a sample may checksum its whole Parquet file. Later selections reuse validation for the unchanged file and use Arrow to filter the cell and prune unrelated row groups before collecting nodes. A checksum scan does not collect the full sample into R. Keep deployed assets read-only; do not disable validation to remove the initial disk scan. Graph preparation stops with exit 137 and no R error Check the host's resource limits before assuming the graph data is corrupt. Use ulimit -t or scheduler diagnostics to check the CPU-time allowance. A full export can hit a time limit even with bounded memory. Do not change shared-host limits. Resume completed samples or submit smaller, sequential cell batches through the existing preparer: Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare_cell_graph_assets.R \ output/proxiomevis_demo_v1.rds /path/to/pxl_directory \ output/hybrid_demo/graphs pixelgen-demo-v1-d20537e8d79c4e12 cells.txt cells.txt contains one exact prepared cell ID per line. Use the dataset ID from your source contract for non-demo data. Each invocation validates and retains previously published cells, atomically rewrites affected sample files with the combined selection, and updates the same index. Run batches sequentially, never against the same directory concurrently. Exit 137 can also indicate a memory limit or an external kill; check the scheduler/system diagnostics rather than repeatedly restarting a healthy process. A worker cannot start or reports a missing package The analysis subprocess uses the app's R installation and library paths. New tests require pixelatorR, Seurat, and SeuratObject; spatial querying also needs Arrow and dplyr. The report-only viewer does not install these optional packages. See Hybrid analysis . Missing worker dependencies or sidecars do not invalidate the frozen reports. Install the required packages in the correct environment, then retry the explicit comparison. The app does not substitute a different test. The worker is busy, times out, or rejects a large selection Only one background analysis runs at a time per Shiny R process , shared by that process's sessions. Busy requests are rejected with a retry message, not queued. Retry after the current job finishes or is cancelled. Closing a session cancels its running analysis. Each job has a 120-second timeout and limits of 2,000 selected cells, 160 markers, 1,000 unordered colocalization pairs, and 1 million retained score rows. Select fewer cells or markers to reduce work; colocalization is limited to 45 markers because 46 produce more than 1,000 pairs. The app never silently downsamples a request. Deployment-level RAM/CPU quotas are still needed: these workload limits are not a memory guarantee, and multiple Shiny processes each have their own worker limit. A new result has missing statistics or differs from the report Abundance requires at least 3 selected cells per condition. Spatial features require at least 20 retained observations per group for self-proximity, or 40 for colocalization. Inspect n_cells_a/b , n_scored_a/b , and status in the result table. Missing or filtered scores are not imputed as zeros, so selecting enough cells does not guarantee every feature is testable. New tests use the submitted cells and eligible selected-marker testing family. Restricting markers can change BH-adjusted p-values even when raw p-values agree with the report. Changing controls does not change the completed result until another run; check its recorded scope and downloaded provenance. Neither result supports population-level inference from cells in a single donor. The bundle or sidecar checksum does not match Reload the trusted dataset if its RDS changed after the app loaded it. Requests are pinned to that loaded file's checksum, not just its dataset name. Sidecars must match the bundle's data and prepared source inputs; do not mix files from different preparation runs or edit checksums to suppress the error. Prepare a new matching bundle in a separate directory when source data changes, and deploy it read-only with its sidecars. A graph is too large or the 3D panel is blank The viewer refuses cells above 200,000 nodes. Select a smaller cell to continue; no nodes are silently dropped. The sidecar and viewer are nodes only: there are no stored edges, edge controls, or marker-count matrices. Plotly 3D requires a browser with working WebGL. Check browser GPU/WebGL support when graph coverage and node totals load but the canvas stays blank. The coordinates are abstract graph-layout positions, not physical microscopy coordinates. The port is unavailable Use another local port, for example: Rscript --vanilla -e 'shiny::runApp(".", host="127.0.0.1", port=3839)' For a shared deployment, keep Shiny behind the environment's authenticated proxy. Do not expose the server-local RDS path control or unrestricted RDS uploads to untrusted users. The server-path field is missing This is the secure default. Configure PROXIOME_PRECOMPUTED_RDS before startup. A trusted local operator can set PROXIOME_ALLOW_LOCAL_LOAD=true to expose the field temporarily. Do not use that flag on a public app.
